page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA extensions. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 1843 GB local SSD and support for Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory performance, particularly in large-block read and write operations, achieving uncached read bandwidth of 230.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 111.32 GB/sec. Most general compute, database, and web serving benchmarks fall within the average range, including a Passmark CPU score of 39,476.15 and Redis SET operations at 38.55 million operations per second. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text generation for large language models represent performance bottlenecks, scoring in the lower quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ds_v4 offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads by bundling substantial local SSD storage with high-capacity RAM, reducing the need for external storage overhead. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable performance. This configuration is highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics pipelines, and enterprise applications requiring high memory density and fast local scratch space.
